  • User choice is optional: Send out the suggestions, but do not require the user to indicate if any of them answered their question.
  • User choice is required: Send out the suggestions, and require the user to indicate if any of the answered their question. Their ticket will be hidden from your techs until the user makes a choice.
If a user indicates that a KB article answered their question, then the ticket will be closed automatically.
section.tips: Enable the KB suggest feature for emails that match this rule? See the help popup for this section for information on what each option means.

section.name: admin_spam_auto_threshold
section.mainhelp:
The threshold settings define how "spammy" a message needs to be for a certain action to be performed.

When a message comes in, the spam filter assigns two probabilities:
  • Probability that the message is good
  • Probability that the message is spam


For example, imagine there is a message that has a good-probability of 0.5 and a spam-probability of 0.58. Technically, the message is considered spam. But the probabilities are so close, it is usually worth passing the message just in case.

So for a message to be marked as spam, the spam filter checks to see if the spam-probability is higher than the good-probability. The threshold settings affect how much higher the spam-probability needs to be.

A threshold of 2 means that the message has to be 2 times more "spammy" than it is good. For example, a message with a good-probability of 0.5 would need a spam-probability of over 1.0 to be considered spam. Anything below 1.0 spam-probability would be given the "benefit of the doubt" and pass the filter.

Notes:
  • The minimum threshold is 1, which means the threshold has no affect on the probabilities.
  • Even small numbers can make a large difference in the outcome. When increasing or decreasing these values, you should try going by tenths. For example, 1.5 to 1.6
  • Depending on the ratio of good-messages to spam-messages, you may need to alter these values from time to time. Generally, a helpdesk that gets much more spam than legit mail will have lower thresholds.
section.tips: The base threshold for detecting any spam (over 1). If a message meets this threshold, the ticket is marked as spam and the user will need to validate themselves. If a lot of spam is coming through, you should decrease this number. If legit messages are being marked as spam, you should increase this number.

The threshold for detecting spam that can be deleted outright (over 1). If a message meets this threshold, the ticket will simply be discarded without ever being saved to the system. This number should be about two numbers higher then the above. You can assign a very high number, like 100, to make sure no ticket is ever deleted automatically.
Disable the spam filter when this rule matches.

section.name: tech_ticketchangeuser
section.mainhelp:
This page allows you to change the user who owns the ticket. This means that the old user will no longer have access to the ticket. Their replies will still be there for techs and the new user to read, but the old user is essentially out of the picture.

This function is useful if you have some automated system that creates tickets on behalf of users (for example, an automated phone system). In such cases, you want to move the ticket to the real users account, not the system account.

section.name: billing_rules
section.mainhelp:
A billing rule is a rule that runs against a user-submitted ticket to determine various costs of support. Costs come in two different types.

Per-ticket costs are charges to the user for every ticket the user submits. The user pays the charge and then the ticket is handled.

Time-interval costs are charges to the user based on time. With these charges, the tech working on a ticket starts a timer. When he has finished, he stops the timer, and then the full amount is calculated and the user is charged.


Rule Chains
Unlike other aspects of DeskPRO, billing rules can be configured to continue even after one rule has been matched. Each subsequent rule that was matched adds to the total charge. Rules are continuously run, one after the other, until the end is reached or until a rule has the 'Is Last' flag enabled.

This chaining allows scenarios where you want to build up the total cost based on various criteria. For example, the category 'Support' might cost $10 per ticket, but if the user choses the 'Emergency' priority, you might want to charge an additional $10.


Canceling Rules with Chaining
To give you more flexibility, you can also define a rule that cancels the effect of a previously matched rule. This can make it easier to create complex chains without needing to create many different rules that branch off for every single scenario. Most of the time, you will not use the canceling functionality.
section.tips: This is a short title or comment to describe the rule. This is used only in the admin interface for describing rules.
This is the cost in credits to charge the user for a new ticket matching this rule.
This is the cost in credits per time interval the user is charged.
This is the order in which this rule will be processed.
When enabled, no other rules will be executed. The charges accumulated up to this rule will be the final charges applied to the user.

You can optionally select any number of other rules that should be reversed (if they were matched at all) when this rule matches. In effect, this essentially makes the system act as if the selected rules were never run at all.

Should this rule set the costs specified instead of add? Normally rules can be run in a chain and accumulate costs of each matched. Using this will disregard whatever total cost was before and set it to the values inputted.
This is the cost of additional replies that is charged to the user when he makes new replies.

section.name: user_plans
section.mainhelp:
A user plan is a plan a user can purchase to give themselves additional access to your helpdesk. You can create special access by using usergroups and permissions, and then a user buys into a user plan which gives them access to the usergroup. Additionally, every plan purchase can optionally come with a set of free credits to give the user.

Free credits reset
If the user renews his subscription to a user plan, the free credits included are not accumulated. For example, if you have a monthly plan that gives a user 20 free credits -- if the user does not use any credits in one month, they do not add up so the next month he gets 40, then 60 etc. They are reset to 20 every month.
section.tips: The title of this plan as seen by users.
A description of this plan as seen by users.
How much this plan costs
How long this plan remains active. After the time runs out, the user will be removed from the usergroup.

section.name: admin_plugin_billing_settings
section.mainhelp:
This page lets you change various billing plugin settings.

"Credits" versus real money
In the system, all values are considered "credits" -- there is no real currency associated internally. This allows the most flexibility. For instance, it allows you to sell 1 credit for $5. Depending on how you wish to market your services, this can be useful.

However, if you don't want to use credits, you can use the settings on this page to indicate all prices to the user in real monetary values. This is the default unless you've changed it. Notice how the credits phrase is simply a dollar symbol, and the credits value is 1. This means a credit is the exact same as a dollar. The helpdesk will then be showing the user these phrases, so it'll appear as all prices are real monetary prices.
section.tips: This defines how to output amounts to the user in web pages (you can use HTML). Since you can configure this plugin to use credits where $1 buys more or less than 1 credit in the system, you may want to change this value to something like "Credits" or "cr" instead of "$" or "dollars" etc. Use the replacement {AMOUNT} for the number.
Same as above except this phrase is used in cases where plain-text is required (like emails).

How much a single credit in the system is worth. This allows you to use "credits" instead of real money to express prices by going above or below a value of 1. For example, a value of 1.5 would mean that $2 buys 3 credits. The word "credits" can be anything you choose with the below options.

The currency to charge users in. Each payment processor will be responsible for converting a users local currency into this currency, you do not need to worry about that. Should be one of: USD, GBP, EUR, CAD, AUD

(Seconds) How the time charges are calculated. That is, the prices you set are charged per time interval. For example, every half an hour, or every hour. It is recommended to keep this as an hourly rate because it is most common. Any time above or below this value will be charged pro-rata.

Round uneven times to the nearest fraction of time. For example, if you charge hourly and want to always calculate costs to the nearest 15 minutes, you would choose 1/4. Thus a work time of 1:55 would be rounded up to 2 hours.
(Seconds) The minimum time to charge. If rounding caused the time to round to 0, or if there was less than this amount of time worked, the time charged will be set to this value.
This defines how to output amounts to the user when you're displaying real money amounts.
Same as above, but this phrase is used in cases where plain-text is required (like emails).
When a user is adding funds to their account, what is the minimum amount of credits they must deposit?
The word to use when describing credits. This is what you want to title credits. For example, "Credits"
The word to use when describing money. This is what you want to title money. For example, "Dollars" or "US Dollars"

Allow a user to change ticket priorities that may affect price? A user will only be able to change the priority before paying for a ticket, or after a tech has already replied (these restrictions prevent users from cheating your prices by "downgrading" their ticket, and then "upgrading" it after paying).

section.name: admin_billing_credit_bundles_list
section.mainhelp: A credit bundle is a bundle of credits the user purchases to get a deal. The more credits he buys, the better of a deal he gets. Use this to entice your users into buying many credits at once

section.name: tech_billing_order_info
section.mainhelp:
This table contains basic information about the order.
  • ID: The ID of the order as it exists in the database. The user does not see or use this ID.
  • Ref: The reference number of the order. This is what the user sees and uses to identify the order.
  • Summary: A one-line summary of the order.
  • Amount: How much the order cost. Depending on how your administrator has configured the helpdesk, you may see a simple dollar amount or an amount in credits. Credits are an internal currency used by the helpdesk to represent value, and can have any real-world monetary value as defined by the administrator.
  • User: The user who owns this order.
  • Created At: When the order was first created.
  • Finished At: If the order was completed (fully paid), the time it was finished.
  • Order Status: The status of the order. Common statuses include pending if the user still needs to pay or complete if the user has paid. The other statuses are only used when you manually chose a status. canceled orders are hidden from users.
  • Processed Status: processed if the order has been processed and changes applied to the user account.

section.name: tech_billing_order_items
section.mainhelp: This table lists the items the order is for. This is the "shopping cart". Though for many features of the helpdesk, only a single item such as a ticket purchase will exist.

section.name: tech_billing_order_trans
section.mainhelp:
This table lists all of the transactions with payment processors related to this order. Note that there may be many listed as 'pending'. This can happen if the user goes through the steps to checkout, but then goes back. Each time the user checks out, a new transaction record is made in preperation for the payment gateway.

While there may be multiple transactions, there will only ever be a single 'completed' transaction. The others exist only for record-keeping.

section.name: admin_user_groups_edit_permsideas
section.mainhelp: This tab lists all of the permissions you can set for this usergroup or company. Permissions are additive. This means that "Yes" will overwrite "No" when permissions are applied to a user. So as long as the user belongs to any usergroup or company that has "Yes" for any given permission, then the user will have that permission.

section.tips: How many votes can a user use on a single idea?
How many votes does a user get to cast before they run out? Note that votes are returned to users once an idea is marked as accepted or declined or completed.
This is a global switch to disable comments on ideas. It will override all usergroup permissions, and will also hide all existing comments in the database (though they won't be deleted).

When enabled, new ideas can be submitted via the AJAX widget you can place on any website. This overrides guest submission permissions and allows anonymous ideas. Anonymous submissions are marked as hidden. Check the online help manual for the feedback plugin for an example of the AJAX widget.

section.name: admin_user_groups_edit_ccemails
section.mainhelp:
You can optionally enter a set of email addresses DeskPRO will CC all ticket notifications to. These people will get notifications for each new ticket and each new reply.

Note that these users only get a plain-text version of the email and won't actually have access to view the ticket online or reply via email. If someone needs access to the ticket, they will have to be added as a ticket participant by a tech or by the ticket owner.
section.tips: Enter which emails you want to CC for this company, one per line.

section.name: admin_template_resources
